role: CV1 / Software Development + Applied AI - system design backbone

headline_finding.claim_tested: Moving the rate-limiter hot path into a C++ extension that releases the GIL will raise gateway throughput.
headline_finding.verdict: FALSE as stated. Releasing the GIL per request is a 12x PESSIMISATION, because the release/reacquire round trip costs far more than the ~200ns critical section it protects. The win is real but comes from compilation, and from amortising the GIL release over a batch - not from releasing it per call.
headline_finding.consequence: gateway/ratelimit/limiter.py calls check_holding_gil on the request path and reserves the GIL-releasing entry point for check_batch. The measurement changed the production code.

second_finding.claim_tested: Flag a client when its anomaly score crosses the threshold.
second_finding.verdict: Per-request scoring false-positives on cold-start transients. Flagging on the MEDIAN of a short score window separated real anomalies from normal clients 6x better on identical traffic.

third_finding.claim_tested: IsolationForest is the right unsupervised detector here.
third_finding.verdict: Only above a real population. Fitted on 5 clients it gave two different anomalies the identical saturated score (0.8049) and a normal client 0.7607 - a 0.04 margin. The robust z-score on the same data separated them by orders of magnitude. The forest is now gated behind min_clients_for_forest=50.

end_to_end.example_reason: sustained 0.87 over 8 requests: request rate unusually high (69.2 MAD); path entropy unusually high (50.0 MAD)

bugs_found_by_running_it: sqlite ':memory:' gives each CONNECTION its own database - a thread-local pool handed every thread an empty one and writes vanished. Fixed with a shared-cache URI.
shared-cache sqlite takes a TABLE lock and returns SQLITE_LOCKED immediately, ignoring `timeout` - 3 concurrent writers dropped rows. Fixed with a write mutex.
a fixed shared-cache NAME made every Store(':memory:') in a process the same database, so independent tests saw each other's rows. Fixed with a per-instance name.
anomaly min_history conflated 'clients needed to fit' with 'observations per client', so 7 real clients never satisfied a threshold of 30 and the detector silently scored everything 0.0 forever.
MAD collapse: when a feature's median is 0 the scale estimate is 0 and every deviation ran to 1e9. Fixed with relative AND absolute scale floors.
integration tests assumed 'no upstream is running' and failed on a machine where the demo services were up. Pinned to dead ports.
known_limits: Rate-limit state is per-process and in-memory. Two gateway replicas enforce two independent limits; a shared Redis or a consistent-hash router is needed before horizontal scaling.
The anomaly baseline is also per-process, so replicas learn different norms.
The IsolationForest path is implemented and tested but does not activate below 50 clients, which the demo does not reach - the measured results are the robust-z detector.
LLM explanations default to offline templates. The Anthropic path is implemented but is only exercised when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set.
Benchmarked on one machine (Apple M-series, CPython 3.13). The GIL result is expected to hold on any CPython with the GIL enabled but has not been re-measured on x86 or on a free-threaded build.
